articleTitle: Circuit modeling of separate absorption, charge and multiplication avalanche photodiode (SACM-APD)
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: We present a circuit model for separate absorption, charge and multiplication avalanche photodiode (SACM-APD). It is based on the carrier rate equations in the different regions of the device. Using the model we obtain the photocurrent, quantum efficiency, and dark current. As examples, GaAs and InGaAs/InAlAs SACM-APDs are simulated. There is a good correspondence between the simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Form parameters definition of optical fibers welded connection
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The control of geometrical parameters of a welding optical fibers place is carried out by a focusing method of a sounding cross beam. The parameters of the form determining losses of optical capacity in the place of welding of optical fibers are considered. The algorithm of the measured image processing of fiber welded connection, distinguishing fiber cladding contours and fiber core axis is offered.

articleTitle: Mathematical modeling of devices for measuring of laser radiation characteristics by wire grids
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Grids from thin metal wires are proposed for measurements of laser power and pulse energy. They may be used for measuring intensity distribution in beam. The main idea is that the wires will change their electric conductivity if they are heated by laser radiation. By placing an array of wires in a laser beam the measurement of the conductivity change of each wire delivers information about the spatial distribution of intensity. The resolution and the total absorption depend on the spatial density of the wires, where a higher density allows a higher resolution, and a lower density allows placing the wire grid directly in the laser beam with very small losses of power and the shape distortion of the beam cross-section.

articleTitle: The modern OCXO quartz oscillators requirements and parameters
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: It seems that in last few years the quartz crystal precision oscillators OCXO did reach the limit of parameters improvement. Most of OCXO designers focused their attention on price reduction and practicability of oscillator construction. In Tele and Radio Research Institute new designs of OCXO oscillators fulfilling requirements of military standard MIL-STD-202G were made. In the paper there are described important requirements for military and civil OCXO oscillators and parameters of new designed oscillators. The results of new elaborated oscillators investigations show that the improvement of OCXO oscillators parameters is still possible.

articleTitle: Transformation of the continuous laser power on wavelength 10.6 microns with thin-wire bolometer
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The aim of this work consists in the determination of the transformation coefficient of the concrete platinum bolometer for continuous laser power on a wavelength 10.6 microns, using the known temperature dependence of a specific resistance of platinum, and the relation (in long-wave approximation) of complex refraction index of platinum with a specific conductivity and with the measured temperature dependence of the coefficient of heat-exchange with an environment.

articleTitle: Quality criterion of radiation in active medium of laser systems with adaptive optics
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Effective beam correction in laser adaptive system is discussed. The hypothesis about the time dependence of correction of wave front from relative entropy angles of an inclination of wave front in the direct ratio is offered. To check this hypothesis imitation modeling of the laser system supplied by an adaptive optical phase conjugation system is carried out. This system was with Hartmann wave front sensor and controlled sectional mirror.

articleTitle: High frequency light self-modulation in simple interference scheme
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The coherent light self-modulation process was studied by modeling the simplest interference scheme containing beam splitting, delaying and amplifying. Principal possibilities of cw laser light passive modulation with GHz-THz frequencies and amplified pulses formation are shown. Some scheme parameters and input light features influence the processes are mentioned above illustrated and discussed.

articleTitle: Optical absorption and luminescence in KDP:XO dye inclusion crystals
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The present work deals with the investigation of potassium dihydrogen phosphate (KDP) single crystals containing xylenol orange dye (XO) by means of optical and luminescence spectroscopy. Investigation shows that XO incorporates in KDP single crystal and occupies oriented sites. It leads to the appearance of the dichroic optical absorption and the polarized luminescence in the visible spectral region.

articleTitle: The mathematical models of problem about wave beams diffraction on a plane metallic grating
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: In this paper received mathematical models of paraxial wave beams scattering by strip gratings for the solution of the Riemann-Hilbert problem method and a method of singular integral equations are used.

articleTitle: Dual band lasing of benzopyrane dye for red spectral region under laser excitation
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This work studies the laser spectrum peculiarities of the benzopyrane dye which have high quantum yield of fluorescence (q /spl ges/0.96) and high-performance lasing under laser pumping as well as flashlamp one. This dye - LD1 differs in that its lasing spectrum consists of two bands in nonselective cavity under laser pumping. Shift distance between the centers of these bands exceeds the full width of them more than twice.

articleTitle: Vortices in laser-type resonators
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This study discusses the characteristics and properties of vortices in laser-type resonators. Various phenomena are also illustrated by experiments on lasers or laser-like systems like photorefractive resonator and by numerical solutions of the corresponding 2D+1 partial differential equations, such as the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation.

articleTitle: Quasi-optical measurement technique for low-loss materials in short millimeter and submillimeter wave ranges
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This study presents a set up for measurement of different low-loss materials and substances (liquid and solid-state dielectrics, ferroelectrics, semiconductors, ferrites, composite, building, nature and commonly used materials and media) in short millimetre (MM) and submillimetre wave (SMM) ranges, mainly at the wavelengths /spl lambda/ = 3.0 - 0.6 mm. This measurement technique for materials investigation in MM and SMM ranges uses quasi-optical lens beam waveguide spectroscopy methods. This version of MM and SMM spectroscopy has some advantages in frequency range 50 - 500 GHz.

articleTitle: Control of influence of Auger recombination on the threshold in asymmetric quantum-well lasers
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: In the work, general description of the Auger recombination (AR) processes in quantum-well (QW) heterostructure is presented and new conception of weakening the temperature sensitivity of the threshold in asymmetric QW heterolasers is suggested. Numerical simulation is approved on an example of the GaInAs-GaInAsP laser system.

articleTitle: A rigorous numerical modeling of exciton electroabsorption in coupled multiple quantum wells modulators
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: In this paper an accurate model for calculation electroabsorption spectrum of CMQWS modulators is proposed. First, the electron and hole subband energy levels and their envelope wave functions are calculated using transfer matrix method (TMM). Next a variational method is used to obtain the exciton binding energy and its wave function. Then electroabsorption spectrum for TE and TM mode of input light is calculated considering band to band and excitonic transitions without any fitting parameter. The broadening of excitonic peak with phonon interaction, applied electric field, well width variation, temperature fluctuation and quasi bound life time is taken into account. Then, numerical results are presented. The results are in good agreement with experimental results reported.

articleTitle: Theoretical investigations of one-dimensional photonic crystal with Kerr nonlinearities
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The paper investigated the properties of the nonlinear one-dimensional photonic crystals such as reflectivity spectra and field distribution with different value of the nonlinear parameter and a number of nonlinear layers.

articleTitle: Simulation of preionization system for XeCl-lasers
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Results of preliminary study of temporal characteristics of the XeCl-laser capacitance preionization are presented. The preionization of active medium is one of the major factors, which determines operation of electric-discharge lasers. The roles played by HCl density as well as optimal delay between the main discharge and auxiliary preionization discharge are investigated.

articleTitle: Analysis of energy-band structure of 1D and 2D photonic crystals by the coupled wave method
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: In this paper the 2D photonic crystal is presented as some number of periodic reiteration of plane diffraction grating (stack of gratings). Computation of transmission of grating stack was conducted by the coupled wave method (CWM). The stable S-algorithm is used for computation.

articleTitle: A semiconductor laser with a fiber ring cavity
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: A novel semiconductor laser with fiber ring resonator is proposed. The experimental setup was assembled to demonstrate the possibility of the laser beam generation. The threshold pumping current value is 60 mA, intermode beat frequency is 50 MHz.

articleTitle: The Coulomb repulsion compensation of the beam ions in the presence of a strong pulsed laser field
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: In this work, the effective interaction force of the classical nonrelativistic hydrogen ions in the beam crossover in the presence of a strong-pulsed laser field is analyzed. It is shown that the effective interaction force of ions may be the attraction force. A practical possibility of compensation of the Coulomb repulsion of the hydrogen ions in the beam crossover region under the influence of strong-pulsed laser field is studied.

articleTitle: Mueller-matrix tomography of biotissue
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Summary form only given. The polarization tomography features of optically anisotropic architectonic nets of different morphological structure biotissues (BT) have been investigated. The phase tomography (PT) features of skin derma, muscular and bone BT have been experimentally investigated. The interrelation between the PT structure and BT physiological state has been determined. The early diagnostics criteria of the degenerative-dystrophic appearance and pathological changes of the structure of BT optically anisotropic architectonics have been determined: (i) Optical anisotropy of physiologically normal myometry is not practically apparent- the PTs represent a quasi-homogeneous field with several fluctuations /spl Delta/n(X,Y) /spl ap/ 10/sup -5/. This points to a rather amorphous optical structure of BT, i.e., to "lack of development" of myometry collagen net. (ii) The phase component topology of the diffusely changed myometry architectonics is formed by the areas with inhomogeneous distribution of birefringence /spl Delta/n(X,Y), the values of which vary from 1.2 /spl times/ 10/sup -4/ to 1.1 /spl times/ 10/sup -3/ respectively. (iii) The tumor-forming processes are accompanied by the formation of "anisotropy zones", within which the birefringence value of architectonics increases by two orders and reaches the level of 2.5 /spl times/ 10/sup -3/.

articleTitle: Modelling the amplitude and phase of plane wave reflected and transmitted by Fabry-Perrot resonator
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The proposed paper summarizes the results of author's studies of Fabry-Perrot interference light by three-layer structures. The structures can be divided into three groups: two unsymmetrical and a symmetrical one.

articleTitle: Mode selection of a linear laser array with an external Talbot cavity
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Summary form only given. Possibility of modes selection of linear laser array with an external Talbot cavity by a method of in-cavity square-low phase corrector is experimentally demonstrated. A conjugated telescope consisting of a cylindrical focusing lens and convex mirror was used as a flat equivalent cavity mirror. Beam matrix of a such telescope coincides at certain distance between mirror and lens with a beam matrix of a Talbot cavity. Change in distance between mirror and lens leads to appearance of the variable radius of curvature of an equivalent mirror that corresponds to insertion of the square-low phase corrector into Talbot cavity. For three element laser array the transition from out-in-phase mode to in-phase mode was observed at subsequent increase of the telescope length as well as at variation of the curvature radius of convex mirror. This change in a generation nature corresponds to changes of the calculated eigenvalues of different modes for empty cavity, which are received for laser array used in an experiment.

articleTitle: Modeling of reflectograms of optical line that includes fibres with different level of Rayleigh scattering
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The Monte-Carlo method is used for the reflectograms simulation in the optic fibre. In the present work numerical simulation of the reflectograms of the optical line that includes fibres with different level of Rayleigh scattering was made by using this method.

articleTitle: Fractal structure of biotissues polarization properties for early diagnostic cancer changes
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The interconnection between geometry of biotissue structure with their polarization properties has been studied. It has been shown that fractal character of polarization properties of physiologically normal biotissue transforms into a multifractal for a pathologically changed one.

articleTitle: On the validity of Rayleigh-Sommerfeld propagation formulas
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Results of simulation by first Rayleigh-Sommerfeld integral formula (RS1),second Rayleigh-Sommerfeld integral formula (RS2) and Helmholtz-Kirchoff integral formula (HK) in studying beam propagation are compared by known rigorous solutions according the Mie theory in spherical coordinates and corresponding more simple expansions in cylindrical 2D-geometry. For simplicity, the monochromatic field propagation in cylindrical coordinates when the beam propagates along x-axis and is homogeneous to z is used. This model well approximates radiation of a most part of diode lasers.

articleTitle: Laser diagnostics of acoustic emission in solids
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The acoustic emission of the ensemble of the growing germs of the new phase in solid, the scattering of hypersonic wave by an indicated ensemble and the transition processes initiated by an hypersonic pulse were investigated. Two characteristic stages of germ formation-initial and late (stage of coalescention) were considered. The analysis of acoustic emission showed, that the ensemble of growing germs generates acoustic waves which frequencies /spl omega//sub /spl Aring// are simply connected with the size R of heterogeneities (germs), and the intensity of each spectral component is determined by their concentration n(R). If we direct a laser beam on the sample, the radiation will be dispersed on the hypersonic waves, and the scattering angle will be simply connected in the frequency of an acoustic wave and therefore with the sizes of a germ R.

articleTitle: On the angular spectra of anti-Stokes stimulated Raman scattering under self-focusing
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: It is shown in this work, by the example of the first anti-Stokes component in toluene, that a high efficiency of conversion of laser radiation into the Stokes component in the focal regions of self-focusing (SF) plays a decisive role in the formation of the angular structure of radiation. The inclusion of a high efficiency of pumping conversion into the Stokes component in SF allows the basic regularities of the formation of the angular structure of an anti-Stokes radiation to be determined. The length of the domain of existence of the nonlinear polarization at the anti-Stokes frequency is expressed in this case in terms of optical parameters of a light-scattering medium, where this quantity is introduced by way of matching the calculated and the observed angles of preferable radiation. Moreover, the longitudinal distribution function of the nonlinear polarization turns out to be distinct from the Gaussian one proposed previously. The results of the calculations carried out are compared with experimental data obtained for toluene in a cell 25 cm long in which SRS was excited by single pulses 20 ns long with an energy of 0.6 J from a ruby laser with passive Q-switching.

articleTitle: Single-mode lightguide with optimized coefficient of optical power localization
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This study takes into account an extremely high price of technological search of lightguides with the given parameters for concrete operations. The described method of lightguide synthesis allows to obtain the law of a refractive index in the cross-section of a lightguide with the given power localization coefficient for a propagated wave on a fixed frequency. To test the proposed method, numerical simulation is carried out using the solution of an analysis problem for synthesized lightguides. The comparison shows that the discrepancy is not more than 0.15%. An application of such lightguides expands functional possibilities of the integrated optical elements, which can be used in various waveguide devices.

articleTitle: The device of measurement of parameters of holograms
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This research developed a pre-production model of the device of measurement of parameters of holographic protective elements (HPE), which allows to find and determine features of optical images in different planes. The device model also aims to distinguish optical images with real spatial depth under the area of the hologram, to define change of images on a corner of supervision (the cinematic effects), to supervise numbering holograms, and to reveal and analyse the latent images. The device allows determining quantitative characteristics, the maximal spatial frequency in the holographic image, the cumulative quantity of the diffraction lattices, the integrated diffraction efficiency or diffraction efficiency of separate, and visually homogeneous elements of the image. The device can be effectively used for the control and measurement of parameters of HPE which have the best level of protection, at carrying out the certified tests in the specialized laboratories' manufacturers of holograms at quality assurance of holographic production, and also supervising bodies.

articleTitle: Fractal method for diagnosis of gas flow according to lidar measurements results
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Results of the experimental research of the display fractal properties of the turbulent gas stream on realization of the photocurrent on an output lidar system are considered. For this purpose on the basis of experimental installation time realizations of the photocurrent are received at sounding the space containing the directed gas stream.

articleTitle: Single-mode optical fibers with optimized dispersion
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The modification of a synthesis method for optical fibres is proposed. Using the given values of phase and group velocities of a spreading mode, the method restores a profile of refractive index in a cross section of a fiber. It is shown, that values of group velocities of a spreading mode on a fixed frequency determine completely the changes of the refractive index, and, therefore, a variance of a dispersion in an optical fiber. Single-mode fibers with the enlarged passband, increased effective area and minimal dispersion in wavelength band 1550 - 1625 /spl mu/k are obtained.

articleTitle: The research of parametric interaction on testing by a probe field
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Summary form only given. The carried out research of parametric interaction at pumping by narrow-band radiation close to transition 3/sup 2/P/sub 1/2/ /spl rarr/ 3/sup 2/S/sub 1/2/ of sodium atom have shown the presence of three spectral lines in a spectrum of a scattered radiation registered on coming out of a heat pipe. Two lines symmetrically displaced from a transition frequency 3/sup 2/P/sub 1/2/ /spl rarr/ 3/sup 2/S/sub 1/2/ are associated with a frequency-nondegenerate four-photon scattering, and the line shifted in the red side- with four-photon mixing on a system quasilevel of sodium atom. The method of probe field was used for the purpose of verification. In experiments with a probe field as testing radiation the wideband emission of a dye luminescence, i.e. continuous spectrum was used. This probe field was collinear with narrow-band emission of dye laser. The concentration of sodium atoms, measured on a method of a total absorption, during experiments was about 10/sup 14/ cm/sup -3/. As buffer gas in a heat pipe with sodium the neon was used on pressure 600 torr. The intensity of the narrow-band laser emission was about 500 kW/cm/sup 2/. The large angular divergence of the radiation coming out of pipe is the characteristic of the one. The radiation was diffused in a cone.

articleTitle: Focusing of different beams by short focus optics
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: In this paper, numerical methods for fast simulation of nonparaxial beam propagation are discussed. For small distances, in the near field or presence of focusing and other optical elements with high numerical aperture have to be used FFT-algorithms or calculation by rigorous expressions, e.g. eigenfunctions expansions. For long distances more effective is algorithm of correction in the space domain. In all cases of nonparaxial beam propagation when the far field distribution isn't limited to a half space, only rigorous solutions of the wave equation are valid.

articleTitle: A simple mode of frequency tuning of the submillimeter laser
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: A simple method of frequency tuning control of the submillimeter laser within the limits of active substance emission band is presented. By this method one can make a tuning of submillimeter lasers with known central frequencies of active substance emission band and there is a possibility of unequivocal tuning at fixed emission line. The tuning is executed by means of the micrometric mechanism of resonator mirror displacement.

articleTitle: About using TV broadcasting satellites for the time scale synchronization
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This paper is about using TV broadcasting satellites for the time scale synchronization. The advantages and disadvantages of satellite systems for precision clock synchronization are also discussed. The various algorithms for synchronization with the use of the satellites are presented as well.

articleTitle: Factor of absorption efficiency of thin platinum cylinder in three-centimeter wave band
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The factor of absorption efficiency (FAE) of a thin platinum cylinder within a three-centimeter wave band was studied. There were some incorrectness in the used measurement procedure consisting in disposition of the cylinder on the unclosed end of a waveguide, but absorbed by the cylinder. Furthermore, high-frequency power was determined on a relative increment of resistance, a temperature coefficient of resistance, and coefficient of the heat exchange with environment. The aim of the work is improvement of the measuring procedure and increase of reliability of the received results.

articleTitle: Transmission of submillimeter laser beams through metal rectangular waveguides
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Theoretical and experimental investigations of submillimeter laser radiation transmission of Gaussian profile are carried out in hollow metal rectangular waveguides for a determination of optimal excitation conditions of the waveguides, undistorted transmission of an initial beam and development of guidelines on use of given waveguides in submillimeter transmission lines.

articleTitle: Optical control of a gaseous nonlinear-absorbance modulator enlightening moment
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: A model describing the kinetic process in a thin layer gas (CO/sub 2/), the laser with gaseous phototropic modulator (BCl/sub 3/) is presented. This model is a one-dimensional monomode photon approximation. The control of the phototropic modulator enlightenment working under the two-level circuit, is possible with the help auxiliary radiation on working wavelength.

articleTitle: Radiation of new structures in paraxial Gaussian-type beams
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Summary form only given. New simple explicit solutions of the paraxial parabolic equation different from the well-known Laguerre-Gauss and Hermite-Gauss types are presented. Starting with the classical fundamental axisymmetric mode g, defined by g = exp(ik/spl rho//sup 2//2/spl zeta/)//spl zeta/, where /spl zeta/ = z /spl epsiv/, with /spl rho/ = /spl radic/(x/sup 2/ + y/sup 2/) and /spl epsiv/ > 0 the arbitrary constant, we seek one class of solutions in the form of u = /spl Psi/(X,Y)g, where X = x//spl zeta/, Y = y//spl zeta/, which gives that /spl Psi/ is the solution of the Laplace equation /spl Psi//sub XX/ + /spl Psi//sub YY/ = 0. Of interest in the paraxial context are only those /spl Psi/, which grow with the transverse distance /spl rho/ is such manner that u/spl rarr/0 as /spl rho//spl rarr//spl infin/. We construct another class of solutions assuming the structure of a more general form, u = /spl Psi/(X,Y,/spl zeta/)g, which gives /spl Psi//sub XX/ + /spl Psi//sub YY/ + 2ik/spl zeta//sup 2//spl Psi/ = 0. Separation of variables provides solutions of the form /spl Psi/ = /spl psi/ (X,Y)exp(-2iK/sup 2///spl zeta/ where K is a new free constant, in general, complex, and /spl psi/ is the arbitrary solution of the Helmholtz equation /spl psi//sub XX/ + /spl psi//sub YY + K//sup 2//spl psi/ = 0. Examples of solutions from the both classes, among which are the Bessel-Gauss beams, will be discussed. Similar approach was recently employed for construction of exact (non-paraxial and non-time harmonic) solutions of the wave equation in the previous reference.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal dynamics of laser beams propagating through sharp discontinuities of non-linear dielectric waveguides
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: In this paper, physical phenomena of spatiotemporal transformation of stationary and non-stationary light beams in dielectric guiding structures with step-like refractive index profile and the Kerr-like non-linearity embedded are investigated. The structures, in particular, are step-like discontinuities in planar and cylindrical waveguides.

articleTitle: New materials for highly efficient acoustooptical operation of high power laser radiation
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Summary form only given. The optical (refractive indices, piezooptic coefficients, optical damage thresholds and the transmission spectra) and the elastic properties of the /spl alpha/-BaB/sub 2/O/sub 4/, /spl beta/-BaB/sub 2/O/sub 4/, Li/sub 2/B/sub 4/O/sub 7/ and CsLiB/sub 6/O/sub 10/ crystals are investigated. It is shown that these crystals possess wide range of transparency (/spl sim/0.2 - 3 /spl mu/m) and high level of the optical damage threshold (e.g. for Li/sub 2/B/sub 4/O/sub 7/ it is 32.2 GW/cm/sup 2/). The components of the elastic matrix C/sub mn/ of these crystals are calculated on the basis of the ultrasonic velocity measurements. The photoelastic coefficients of the borate crystals are calculated on the basis of piezooptical coefficients measured with interferometric technique. Using the determined values of the refractive, elastic and photoelastic tensor components, we have calculated the values of the acoustooptic figure of merit M/sub 2/ for these crystals. The acoustooptical figure of merit of /spl alpha/-BaB/sub 2/O/sub 4/ and LiB/sub 4/O/sub 7/ crystals achieve value M/sub 2/ = 243.4 /spl times/ 10/sup -15/ s/sup 3//kg and M/sub 2/ = 2.57 /spl times/ 10/sup -15/ s/sup 3//kg at the interaction with the slowest ultrasonic waves /spl nu/ = 933.5 m/s and /spl nu/ = 3173 m/s, respectively. The acoustooptical modulators on the base of /spl alpha/-BaB/sub 2/O/sub 4/ and LiB/sub 4/O/sub 7/ crystals have been constructed and performance characteristics have been obtained experimentally.

articleTitle: Bright and dark spatial solitons in parametrically driven nonlinear interferometers
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This study deals with bright and dark spatial solitons in parametrically driven nonlinear interferometers. Results of numerical modeling show that couples of bright and dark cavity solitons can be formed in transverse intensity profiles of counterpropagating beams by strong local intensity fluctuations as well as the rest of so-called labyrinthine optical patterns. The final configurations consists of a pair of bright and dark solitons of different order.

articleTitle: Intensity noise in mode-locked external cavity laser
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Effect of spontaneous and carrier noise on mode-locked HSPS utilizing linearly chirped fiber Bragg grating is investigated by using coupled mode-equations. It is found that transform-limited pulses are generated over a wide tuning range without noise and with low noise level. However, mode-locking is difficult to achieve for large value of spontaneous coupling factor and some value of rf and dc currents because of increasing noise. High noise introduce noise peak in the relative intensity noise (RIN) spectrum making transform-limited pulses unobtainable. Hence, proper mode-locking range that transform-limited pulses are generated reduces.

articleTitle: Covering thickness measurement by photothermal method
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: In the present work, the high speed photothermal method is offered. In this method a photothermal response in time after the irradiation of sample by one short impulse is registered. For method realization the heat distribution theory in sandwich-type systems is developed and software for the design of thermal response after laser impulse irradiation (with given parameters) on such systems is created. The simulated temporal changes of temperature on the surface of steel sample covered by one varnish layer after its irradiation by 0.1 /spl mu/s laser impulse with energy density of 1 Dg/sm/sup 2/ is also discussed. Use of speed detectors for registration of thermal response from the surface of the explored sample and use of the developed software allows to define its thickness at the known optical and physical parameters of covering.

articleTitle: Polarized cartography of biofractals
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Specific features of the formation of local and statistical polarization structures of laser radiation scattered in phase-inhomogeneous layers (PIL) of biological tissue (BT) were studied. The distribution of azimuth and eccentricity of boundary field polarization was found to correlate with the orientation-phase structure of multifractal PIL. A method of polarization phase reconstruction of BT architectonics was suggested.

articleTitle: Application of the holographic phase contrast method for 3D imaging of phase micro-objects
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This study presents the results of application of the holographic phase contrast method for computer 3D imaging of native blood erythrocytes. In this method, phase contrast is obtained by holographic addition and subtraction of perturbed waves by the micro-objects and unperturbed waves of equal intensities in interference fringes. From the presented results, it can be concluded that the holographic phase contrast method can be effectively used for 3D imaging of phase micro-objects. The holographic interference microscope with computer processing of interferograms can be an effective device for the purposes of medical diagnostics and scientific investigations.

articleTitle: Resonance scattering of a photon by an electron and resonance radiation of two photons by an electron in the strong magnetic field
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Calculation of the probabilities of quantum electrodynamic (QED) processes in the strong magnetic field is performed, which is important in the ultraquantum case, where inclusion of higher-order processes of the perturbation theory are in resonance conditions.

articleTitle: The light amplification in the scattering of relativistic electron by a nucleus in the light wave field
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This work investigates the gain coefficient in the Coulomb scattering of the relativistic electrons in the medium region of a circularly polarized electromagnetic wave. This study focuses on the stimulated bremsstrahlung and absorption by a relativistic electron scattered by a nucleus in the light wave field.

articleTitle: Influence of dissolution of oxygen on absorption capability of a surface of tantalum
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This research shows the changes of the absorption ability of the surface of tantalum foil when it is heated by means of continuous-wave CO/sub 2/ laser in the air at temperature 600/spl deg/C - 650/spl deg/C. The absorption ability of the sample (when it was completely cooled down after the laser heating) is evaluated by measuring the slope angle of the foil surface temperature growth under the testing laser beam. This study also performed experiments where the heating of one sample is interrupted at definite period of time and the magnitude of absorption capacity is measured. The measurement of Wickers microhardness in surface districts which had undergone laser heating is also conducted.

articleTitle: Laser configurations for high-order transverse mode selection and coherent beam combining
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The paper briefly reviews two different approaches of obtaining high laser output powers with good beam quality. The first approach is operating a laser with a single high-order transverse mode, so that high output power is obtained, followed by efficient external mode conversion to obtain a nearly Gaussian beam. In this approach single high-order mode operation is achieved by inserting phase elements within the laser resonator, so as to introduce high losses to the undesired modes and low losses to the desired mode. Once a single high order mode beam is obtained, with well defined phase and amplitude distributions, external mode conversion by means of phase or interferometric elements can be performed. The second approach is efficient phase locking and coherent addition of several high-quality and low-power laser channels within a laser resonator, to obtain a single high-quality and high-power output beam. With this approach, self phase locking and coherent addition is achieved by use of intra-cavity interferometric combiners, so as to obtain a compact, stable and practical configuration.

articleTitle: Modeling of diode laser cavity under the condition of above-threshold operation
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: A menu-driven computer program is developed for numerical simulations of diode lasers. Three-dimensional structures of typical single-mode lasers are considered. A beam propagation method being employed for the wave (Helmholtz) equation leads to the so-called round-trip operator which is non-linear due to gain saturation and thermal effects. Thus, the main problem for numerical modelling of lasing is the eigen-value problem for the round-trip operator. Special iterative procedure is applied for calculation of a lasing mode under the assumption of potential instability. A large size 3D numerical mesh is employed to discretize a set of equations describing the propagation of two counter-propagating waves using Fade approximation, lateral diffusion of charge carriers within a quantum well, and thermal conductivity. To calculate the injection electric current, at which additional lasing modes appear, the numerical code incorporates a subroutine that calculates a set of possible competing modes using gain and index variations produced by the oscillating mode. The corresponding linear eigen-problem is solved by the Arnoldi method. If all higher-order modes have eigen-values of amplitude less than 1 then the oscillating mode is stable, else we have the unstable mode. Results of numerical simulations for typical experimental conditions will be presented.

articleTitle: Resonance absorption of electromagnetic waves in the system (dielectric grating on metal)
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The effect of full absorption is explained by the appearance of the coupled wave resonance. This effect can be explained in the thermoelectric photodetector of the laser radiation or for the design of the high-directional and high-sensitive antennas in a microwave band. In this case the dielectric grating operates a matching link between impedance of vacuum and impedance of flat the metallic surface.

articleTitle: Peculiarities of the radiation spectra of electrons moving in a spiral in magnetic fields
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Peculiarities of the radiation spectra of two electrons moving one by one in a spiral in vacuum can be investigated combining analytical and numerical methods. Investigations of the radiation spectra of the charged particles moving in magnetic fields in transparent isotropic medium and in vacuum offer practical applications in electronics, astrophysics, plasma physics, and physics of storage rings.

articleTitle: Compact electric-discharge excimer lasers
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The electrodischarge XeCl-laser with a UV-preionization was developed. Preliminary experiments on the effect of UV-radiation of the XeCl-laser on the surface of different polymer coatings were carried out with the purpose of increase of their adhesion to substrates and endurance. The influence of UV-radiation of the XeCl-laser on the surface of different metals is investigated for magnification of their surface hardness, endurance and microhardness.

articleTitle: Simplified model for XeCl-lasers
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The simplified kinetic model for electric-discharge XeCl-laser is presented. According to the solutions of Boltzmann equation for electrons in constant electrical field and calculation of kinetic processes, the major chemical species and kinetic processes were taken into account in our simplified kinetic model. The model enables to calculate an electrons concentration, density of excimer XeCl molecules and specific energy deposition in the active medium.

articleTitle: Laser model for nucleus dissociation
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: In the present paper the laser nonstationary treatment is applied to phase transitions (PT) in alloys, namely to a nucleus dissociation under heating. The nucleus are considered as a new phase rich to one sort of atoms. Electronic states are replaced by atomic states in a crystal lattice site. The inverse population is considered as extra concentration of one sort of atoms and its energy in nucleus after fast heating. Photons are replaced by phonons. Phenomenological equations for phonon and concentration evolution are derived and analysed.

articleTitle: Resonant scattering of a photon by an electron in the laser field
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The appearance of resonances in a laser field is one of the fundamental problems of quantum electrodynamics of strong fields. This research generalizes the results of studies on resonances in Compton processes in the external electromagnetic wave to a general relativistic approach. In this paper relativistic units /spl planck/ = c = 1 are used.

articleTitle: Optical design of four-filter colorimeter
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This study discusses the optical design of a four-filter colorimeter. The design principles and components of the entire system are also emphasized. The instrument is applicable for measuring photometric quantities and optical testing of LCD modules to ensure product quality including the uniform color and luminance of displays and indicators.

articleTitle: Some features of reflectograms of optical lines containing fibres with different apertures
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The Monte-Carlo method is used for the reflectograms simulation in the optic fibre. In present work numerical simulation of reflectograms of optical line that includes fibres with different numerical apertures was made by using this method.

articleTitle: Two-photon pair annihilation in the wave field
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This paper deals with resonant two-photon annihilation of e/sup -/e/sup +/ pair in the field of plane circularly polarised light wave. It is emphasized that the range of resonances is a substantially relativistic domain. For this reason, this article is mainly concentrated on the studies that use a general relativistic approach.

articleTitle: Program interface of the four-channel colorimeter
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The purpose of the project was the development of small-sized, inexpensive industrial colorimeter, which would be simple in manufacturing and using, would have high accuracy and could be produced in lots for maintenance of need for CRT production. The working principle of the developed colorimeter and the computer software for the colorimeter are briefly described.

articleTitle: Computer modeling of fiber-optical and integrated-optical structures
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Finite-difference techniques in the frequency domain (FDFD) method was used for calculation of the integrated-optical structure. As an example of the structure the signal distribution between optical waveguides linked by the ring resonator was investigated. The amplitude-frequency dependence for the structure was calculated with a spectral method. The used method allows to calculate not only exact position of spectral components, which correspond to the same one calculated analytically, but can also predict the relation between amplitudes of spectral components.

articleTitle: Analysis of photopolymerization processes influence on kinetics of transmission grating record in photopolymeric materials
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This work presents the model of the record of 3-dimensional transmission gratings at 0<k<1 and h = 1+k (k- exponent of intensity and h- the exponent of monomer concentration in photopolymerization equations). The comparison of kinetics of transmission gratings record in this kind of photopolymers and its diffraction performances for the optional value of k (0<k<1) are carried out on the base of the numerical simulation. The model also takes into consideration the following factors: polymerization and diffusion mechanisms of record, the photo-induced optical absorption, and the change of diffusion coefficients during the record according the polymerization level.

articleTitle: 2D phase tomography of biotissues for diagnosing their pathologic changes
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The polarization tomography features of optically anisotropic architectonic nets of biotissues (BT) for different morphological structure have been investigated. The phase tomography features (PT) of the skin derma, muscular and bone BT have been experimentally investigated as well. The interrelation between the PT structure and BT physiological state has been determined. The early diagnostics criteria of the degenerative-dystrophic appearance and pathological changes of the BT optically anisotropic architectonics structure have been determined.

articleTitle: Direct determination of the on-axis intensity maximum of diffracted Gaussian beams
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: In lasers, the use of diffracting apertures involves many effects and applications. This goes from the selection of only one eigenmode to oscillate inside the resonator, often called the fundamental mode, the discrimination of the opposite travelling waves within ring resonators, to the control of the beam parameters like diffraction losses, the phase shift and the angular divergence. However, diffraction upon the aperture edge shifts along the optical axis the diffracted beam waist from the position where it would occur for a non apertured beam. The determination of the axial position of the beam waist is important insofar as it indicates the adequate position, inside the resonator, for small amplifying or absorbing media. Realizing that there is no effective treatment of this issue anywhere in literature, we attempt, in this work, to establish formulae which give the axial position for the effective waist of a diffracted beam by one aperture. This position will be expressed as a function of the beam parameters as well as those of the aperture.

articleTitle: Relaxed optics: the problem of the creation and modelling the coherent structures
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The problem of the creation the coherent structures (CS) in relaxed optics (RO) is the one of the general problem of this chapter of modern physics. Coherent structures are called new phases of the matter, with were created after laser irradiation. Practically these are the "traces" of the interaction laser irradiation and matter in matter. These structures may be classified as first-order and second-order structures. One has various energic and time conditions of the creation and stability. The problem of the classification and modelling of these structures may be resolved with the help of short-range, long-range action and mixed approximations of the interaction light and solid. Basic results of these classification and some results of modelling CS are discussed and analyzed.

articleTitle: On relative monochromatic of laser radiation was undergone quasistationary self-focusing
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This work offers a more realistic model of phase modulation under quasistationary self-focusing. The full spectrum is obtained for self-focusing laser radiation pulses which have passed through the Kerr environment of definite length. The spectrum has a complex character with a lot of oscillations. This study also shows that the effect of group delay, in spite of the fact that it has essential value for calculation of focal area speed, and its position does not influence on resulting laser radiation spectrum.

articleTitle: Optical microscopy of the quasiperiodic structures of waveguide nature in AgCl-Ag films
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: We propose the advanced technique for the formation of quasiperiodic structures (QPS) observable by an optical microscope. These structures are induced in photosensitive AgCl-Ag films by linearly polarized Gaussian laser beam with /spl lambda/ = 633 nm. We show that QPS with periods d > /spl lambda/ are effectively developed by excitation of the waveguide TM/sub 0/-modes at great incidence angle and P-polarization of beam. We also show that irradiation of the film attached to 60/spl deg/ glass prism by P-polarized beam incident from glass side causes the growth of the primary C-gratings and secondary slant structures on the TM/sub 0/-modes.

articleTitle: The algorithm treatment optimization of the double beam laser vibrometer signal for large vibration amplitude
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Double beam probing and algorithm treatment are described, which give the possibility to extend the potential of the laser vibrometer in the large amplitude vibration mode.

articleTitle: The comparative analysis of radiometeor and GPS methods of synchronization of time scales
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This study presents methods that provide the time and frequency standards comparison accuracy in the nanosecond limits. But there are different complications in the usage of some or the other methods. Hence, one should always be guided not by the considerations of achieving the maximum accuracy, but by the practicability of the usage of some of the methods in the particular situation when choosing the synchronization method. This work advises to unite several synchronization methods in order to increase reliability. For example, it is recommended to combine radio meteoric method of synchronization (RMS) and satellite radionavigating systems (SNRS) time and frequency scales synchronization systems. Both mutual calibration and examination of both systems results allows to achieve higher synchronization precision.

articleTitle: Experimental research of a parametric scattering of a narrow-band laser radiation in sodium vapor
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The experimental research of non-linear optical processes was held at interaction of the strong resonance emission with a quantum system of a V-type. The vapor of sodium atoms were used as the given system. The energy level scheme of a sodium atom was also discussed.

articleTitle: Influence of two-dimensional Bragg's diffraction on competition of TE/sub 0/and TM/sub 0/-modes at spontaneous grating formation in thin AgCl-Ag films
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This study investigates spontaneous structures arising in waveguide AgCl films doped by Ag. When the film is irradiated by single laser beam with a wavelength in the visible light range (He-Ne laser, /spl lambda/ = 632.8 nm), Ag granules scatter the beam (Rayleigh scattering). AgCl is a dielectric with large forbidden gap, so it does not absorb visible light and therefore does not participate in scattering. Furthermore, this spontaneous structure acts as an imperfect diffraction grating and may be characterised by a set of micrograting vectors determined as differences between mode vector and tangential component of incident wave. The main result of this work is the discovery of the two-dimensional Bragg's diffraction influence on micrograting interaction in their development. This diffraction on a dominant grating simultaneously amplifies two other microgratings which can also become dominant.

articleTitle: Evolution of the radiation spectrum of tunable dye laser at the microsecond pulses
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The process of formation of the spectrum of a flash-lamp-pumped tuned dye laser (DL) is studied. The dependence of the lasing wavelength on parameters of an active medium and resonator is found. It is shown, that inhomogeneous distribution of the triplet-triplet absorption in the selective resonator can result in a modification not only spectral, but also temporary characteristics of the pulse radiation of DL.

articleTitle: Complete 3D-analysis method of spatial anisotropy of acoustooptical interaction for example of /spl beta/-BaB/sub 2/O/sub 4/ crystals
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This study developed a new computer aided method in geometry optimization of electro- or acoustooptical interaction based on spatial anisotropy complete 3D-analysis of electro- or acoustooptical effect in crystal materials. This method allows substantially improving an efficiency of such modulators and has been used by us for geometry optimization of acoustooptical interaction in /spl beta/-BaB/sub 2/O/sub 4/ crystals, which are a promising acoustooptical material.

articleTitle: System of measurement of optical frequencies of the standard of frequency (length of a wave) national standard of unit of length of Ukraine
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This work focuses on the system of measurement of optical frequencies of the standard of frequency national standard of unit of length of Ukraine. In the present study, the case when used femtosecond laser frequencies f/sub r/ and f/sub ceo/ are known and stabilized is considered. In this case the design of a developed measuring complex will include heterodyne optical fiber system of registration and processing of beat signals.

articleTitle: The role of caustics in formation of network of amplitude zeroes in speckle field
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The topology of a partially developed speckle field is studied using interference techniques. It has been shown that formation of interference forklets in the field gives evidence of changes in the field topology, being the diagnostic sign of transition from a planar Fraunhofer diffraction pattern to a three-dimensional pattern of a diffraction catastrophe.

articleTitle: Accurate measurement of the radius of curvature of laser mirrors using mode crossing in marginally unstable laser resonator
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This paper studies the phenomenon of the eigenmodes crossing in the marginally unstable semispherical resonator. The integral equations method is used for the problem statement.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of laserotherapy for the treatment of the patients with primary hypothyroidism and ischemic heart disease
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The efficiency of application of the low-intensive laser therapy for the patients with the primary hypothyroidism and ischemic heart disease (IHD) is studied.

articleTitle: Dynamical behaviour of holographic polymer-liquid crystal gratings
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: In view of POLICRYPS (an acronym for polymer-liquid crystal-polymer slices) optimisation, this study analyses the dynamical response of POLICRYPS gratings and its relation with some geometrical and morphological factors. The final goal is to get overall response times in the sub-millisecond range. Results show that even for not-optimised grating samples, it was possible to get simultaneously both rise and fall response times in the range 50-150 /spl mu/s by means of a proper choice of the driving pulse shape. These results are very attractive for many possible applications in telecom devices.

articleTitle: Broadband optical and wireless networking - an evolutionary approach
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: A combination of different technologies as connection and connectionless networks, optical cable and wireless suitable for a variety of purposes and services in order to achieve global broadband networking features is proposed. The new network model contains an extension to wireless world in order to achieve mobility and personalisation of the connection. From the network point of view it contains an upgrade of real-time traffic with the microwave modulated optical wave, in order to carry out conventional mobile via optical fibres through long distances and without a significant distortion.

articleTitle: Dark spatial solitons in semiconductor microcavities
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This study reports the characteristics of dark solitons different from bright solitons. A striking feature of dark solitons observed in this work is a reflectivity higher than 1 at the center of the soliton. The reflectivity higher than 1 results because the soliton collects energy from its surrounding. As has been predicted for bright solitons this constitutes an optical amplification mechanism worthwhile considering for technical applications. Results show that in addition to the differential gain predicted for bright solitons, the dark solitons experimentally observed permit "DC gain", i.e. the reflected intensity is higher than the incident intensity. Thus dark solitons show "absolute" gain.

articleTitle: Evaluation of properties of microlens manufactured from photopolymerised drops
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Summary form only given. For research of optical properties of microlens made by method of photopolymerisation of sessile drop the interference method on base of Mach-Zehnder interferometer is used. Task is leads to determination of properties of microlens, which have deviation from ideal lens shape. Microlens made from drops of photopolymerised compositions have some imperfection: not well-defined aperture stops, which depend on quality and cleanness of substrate; not absolute spherical surfaces, which depend on drop shape formed in gravitation field; some inhomogeneity of refraction index that is concerned with speed of drop hardening process. In that case a question arises: How should the microlens be used in order to obtain optimum lens properties? Used interferometric method gives the phase distribution of light beam behind lens in every point of beam propagation. It allows: to calculate the longitudinal spherical aberration; using Rayleigh's criterion to calculate a number aperture and focal distance that determine conditions for the smallest focal spot size; to calculate the intensity distribution in a focal plane that is direct related with imaging properties of microlens.

articleTitle: Correlation structure of Mueller matrices of biotissue and their physiological state diagnostics
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The interrelation of orientation, anisotropy structure of biotissue architectonics and topological element distribution of John's matrices is investigated here. The analytical correlation of bioobject John's matrices microstructure with matrix element indices measured in the far field of Fraunhofer's diffraction is researched. The investigation is also dealt with the computer modeling and experimental researching the structure of matrix operator of multifractal amorphous-crystalline organization of different morphological structure biotissues.

IEEE Keywords: Active matrix organic light emitting diodes

articleTitle: Communication modes for information content analysis
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Approximate modes which give physical understanding for the communication modes theory,are discussed. For the geometry consisting of two line or square apertures, perpendicular to the optical axis, this approximation leads to exactly the same modes as Gabor's theory would yield.

articleTitle: The equivalent electrical circuits of semiconductor lasers with quantum wells
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: In work, the principle of construction of electrical models of semiconductor injection lasers with quantum-dimensional structures is considered. On an example models developed before, the equivalent circuit of the semiconductor injection laser with quantum wells is considered.

articleTitle: Cs/sub 2/BX/sub 4/(B=Cd, Hg; X=Br, Cl) crystals- highly efficient acoustooptical materials
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Summary form only given. The photoelastic and acoustooptical parameters of Cs/sub 2/HgBr/sub 4/ and Cs/sub 2/CdBr/sub 4/ crystals are determined on the base of study of the thermal expansion, optical indicatrix rotation at ferroelastic phase transition and direct piezooptical measurements. It has been shown that Cs/sub 2/HgBr/sub 4/ and Cs/sub 2/CdBr/sub 4/ crystals are good acoustooptical materials. The photoelastic coefficients of Cs/sub 2/HgBr/sub 4/ and Cs/sub 2/CdBr/sub 4/ crystals achieve values p/sub 44/ = 0.12 and p/sub 44/ = 0.2 respectively as well as acoustooptical figures of merit- M/sub 2/ = 126.5 /spl times/ 10/sup -15/ s/sup 3//kg for Cs/sub 2/HgBr/sub 4/ crystals and M/sub 2/ = 366.9 /spl times/ 10/sup -15/ s/sup 3//kg for Cs/sub 2/CdBr/sub 4/ crystals. Acoustooptical diffraction has been observed and studied experimentally in Cs/sub 2/HgCl/sub 4/, Cs/sub 2/HgBr/sub 4/ and Cs/sub 2/CdBr/sub 4/ crystals. From the studied range of transparency (/spl sim/0.32 /spl mu/m-20 /spl mu/m) follows that all three crystals can be used as effective acoustooptical materials in the wide spectrum range.

articleTitle: Diffraction of a Gaussian beam by the optical wedge system
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This paper aims to study the physical mechanism of the high effective generation of high-order optical vortices by the optical wedge system. Results of experimental and theoretical studies have shown an opportunity of formation of structurally steady high-order optical vortices by the optical wedge system.

articleTitle: Intensity modulation of hybrid soliton pulse source
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The resonance peak spectral splitting in the intensity modulation of the hybrid soliton pulse source that the fiber Bragg gratings are used as an external cavity can be suppressed by introducing suitable linear chirp rate in the Gaussian apodized grating.

articleTitle: Analysis of reflection properties of Bragg mirror with oxide window
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: In present high-reflectivity laser reflectors are usually made of number of quarter-wavelength Bragg stacks. This is done for necessary reflectivity and operating range. Because of the periodicity of the quarter-wavelength structure, these reflectors have non-zero reflection delay and phase dispersion. The dispersion leads to the impulse widening and distortion. The delay leads to the increasing of the pulse traveltime in the resonator. The investigations of such phenomena in laser reflectors are extremely important in VCSELs with oxide window because of their application in data transfer systems with high bit rate. The oxide window has an influence on the electromagnetic field distribution is laser cavity and it can be the source of the additional dispersion. That's why the analysis of Bragg mirrors with oxide window reflectivity is the topical problem.

articleTitle: On the prospects of diagnostic of wave dislocation
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: The possibility of application of the edge and screw dislocations of the field, obtained in polychromatic light for diagnostics of different phase-inhomogeneous structures, including nanostructures has been considered.

articleTitle: Light beams self-trapping process stability in transparent photopolymerizable compositions
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Numerical and experimental analysis of threadlike heterogeneities formation in waveguiding structures formed at the optical beam self-trapping process in photopolymerizable compositions is conducted. The conditions of homogeneous waveguiding channel formation are determined and confirmed by experimental results.

articleTitle: Broadband diffractive optics
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This article examines how polarization modulation can be exploited, not only to increase the diffraction efficiency, but also how it can be used to extend the known optical designs made for narrow-band light to hold also for the broadband radiation.

articleTitle: Mathematical models applied to optical and thermal diagnostic of semiconductor heterostructures and lasers
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Calculations were done for semiconductor heterostructures, InGaAs quantum well surrounded by GaAs waveguide layers and AlGaAs cladding layers. Finite difference method is used in solving Schrodinger equation. Temperature of the laser active region is measured. The method is based on the theory of current flow through the p-n junction. The laser mirror is investigated by thermoreflectance mapping. The method is a modulation technique, which allows for obtaining a 2-dimensional map of temperature of resolution up to single microns.

articleTitle: Nonradiative energy transfer in 2D ordered organic structures
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This work concerns theoretical studying of excitation energy transfer in the ordered multilayer organic films, doped with active luminophore molecules. Such ordered structures can be formed using modern techniques of molecular electronics: Langmuir-Blodgett, self-assembly, ionic self-assembly etc. In such systems of doped matrix, where no immediate contact between donor and acceptor molecules exist, the most considerable way of energy transfer is the Forster transfer. It involves the through-space interaction of the excited donor molecule with a neighboring acceptor molecule.

IEEE Keywords: Active matrix organic light emitting diodes

articleTitle: High-speed holographic visualisation of processes in transparent media
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: A fast holographic cinematography method was used in the investigation of optical inhomogeneities in transparent media (plasma, gases and liquids, including active media of lasers, transparent solids). Experiments showed that the relaxation of active media of dye lasers with flash lamp excitation has the form of pulses representing a sequence of the appearance and decay of inhomogeneities which are optically equivalent to a spherical lens with a focal length that increases from one period to the next.

articleTitle: Optically coupled lasers
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Results on phase locking of optically coupled waveguide CO/sub 2/ lasers are presented. The optical coupling is an effective method for the chaos synchronization in a chaotic lasers.

articleTitle: Large aperture deformable bimorph mirrors
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Bimorph mirrors as wavefront correctors used in laser adaptive system and their types together with their main features are discussed.

articleTitle: Radiative recombination and transport processes in optochemotronic devices with well ordered monomolecular LB film structures
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Mechanism of charge transfer in the system with well ordered structure, such as Langmuir-Blodgett (LB) film, rises by electrogenerated chemiluminescence (ECL) reaction in the analytical systems, such as optochemotronic sensor, is demonstrated. Estimating curves of that process are presented.

articleTitle: The influence of space charge on spatial resolution of a nuclear microprobe
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This paper is devoted to the theoretical study of the influence of the space charge on broadening of the protons beam of a nuclear microprobe. The nonrelativistic proton beam, having energy about 1 MeV is investigated. The paraxial beam characterized by small radius and small slope angles of trajectories is considered. The change of the mechanical trajectory of the proton in the radial direction evoked by the spatial charge distributed in some conical volume according to the assigned law is also considered.

articleTitle: Thermal energy coupling to Al in ablation with ms-, ns-, and fs-laser pulses
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Residual energy coefficient defined as the ratio of thermal energy retained in aluminum sample following laser ablation to the energy of incident laser radiation as a function of laser fluence was studied. Experiments were performed in various gas media with the use of ms-and ns-ruby, ns-Nd:glass, and fs-Ti:sapphire lasers. For ns- and fs-laser pulses an abrupt significant rise of residual energy coefficient of aluminum occurs above the ablation threshold in a gas medium and does not occur in vacuum. For ms-laser pulses the residual energy coefficient increases slightly both in air and vacuum in the range of laser fluences above the ablation threshold.

articleTitle: Ultimate information-rate density of chromium-doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: This work compares ultimate high-rate characteristics of common used erbium-doped fiber amplifiers and chromium-doped ones within the framework of the number-state model. Chromium-doped fiber amplifiers are new kind of optical fibers with the reduced absorption of hydroxyl group with passband widths up to 400 nm.

articleTitle: Simulation of polarization mode dispersion in optical waveguide
publicationTitle: 6th International Conference on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling, 2004. Proceedings of LFNM 2004.
abstract: Simulation of polarization mode dispersion in optical waveguide in supposition, that sections of optical fiber with determinate of orientation of a core ellipticity have an identical length is described in the work. Also orientation of ellipticity of core cross-section on each section and value its of ellipticity remain stationary values. At calculations it was supposed, that the orientation of ellipse axes of core cross-section of each consequent section of a fiber is determined according to the random law in relation to orientation of axes of the previous section. The signal propagating in optical waveguide represented as a linearly polarized light wave. Since real fibres cannot be perfectly circular and can undergo local stresses; consequently, the propagating linearly polarized light wave is split into two local polarization modes propagating at different velocities. The difference of group velocities is determined by difference of numerical values of ellipse axes and is a cause of a polarization mode dispersion.
